topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D Intuition
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) with basic calculus and linear algebra background

sections.title: Introduction: The Curse of Dimensionality
lecture_lines: Generalizing, spheres in n-dimensions live in R^n.
Points distance r from origin: sum x_i^2 = r^2.
animations: Show a large volume hypercube [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] with a small central region. Color the hypercube #FFFFFF and the inner shell #FF4500.
Illustrate the concentration of volume in the corners. Use Dot objects to fill corners in #00CED1.
Highlight that high dimensions feel empty. Use fade-out of central volume #FF4500 to show sparsity.
Emphasize the distance between points grows. Draw arrows between points #FFD700.

Conclude with the paradox of the 'hollow' high-dimensional space. Fade in text 'Empty Space' #FFFFFF using the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] to represent the shell.

sections.title: Scaling Geometry: Volume vs. Surface Area
lecture_lines: Volume and surface area change as dimensions increase.
Gamma function Γ(n) generalizes factorials for high dimensions.
As n grows, unit sphere volume tends toward zero.
animations: Show a square (2D) and a sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] (3D). Use #FFD700 for the square and #FF4500 for the sphere.
Demonstrate the shrinking volume ratio as dimensions increase. Use a shrinking Dot #FFFFFF.

Finalize the visual comparison between interior and surface volume. Compare Square and Sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] in grid D3 and D4 using colors #FFFFFF and #00CED1.

sections.title: The 'Spiky' Phenomenon: Where is the Volume?
lecture_lines: High-dimensional spheres concentrate volume near the surface.
Imagine an orange: the peel holds the mass.
animations: Draw a 'spike' protruding from the center of a hypercube, utilizing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg] to represent the spike. Color spike #FF4500.
Show the volume concentrating at the spikes. Use flashing effect on spike #00CED1.
Explain why intuition fails in higher dimensions. Overlay text 'Intuition Gap' #FFD700. Use [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg] as a visual anchor for the concept.

sections.title: Application: Why this matters in Data Science
lecture_lines: Euclidean distance loses meaning in high dimensions.
User preferences form points in 1,000-dimensional space.
animations: Visualize high-dimensional data points using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/user.svg] as data representatives. Use many small Dots #FFFFFF.
Display a distance metric calculation: d(x,y). Use MathTex #FFFFFF.
Show how nearest neighbors become equidistant. Color neighbor Dots #FF4500 and #FFD700.

sections.title: Conclusion: Developing Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: Trust algebraic definitions over spatial intuition.
Data points scatter into high-dimensional voids.
animations: Summarize the shift from low to high-dimensional thinking. Use a transition animation between a 2D square and an n-dimensional [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg]. Color change #FFFFFF to #FFD700.
Reiterate the importance of geometric intuition. Flash text 'Geometric Intuition' #00CED1.

Final visual synthesis of all key concepts. Display all elements ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg], [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg], spikes) in a grid #FFFFFF.
